question.problem: Find the roots of the polynomial $p(x)=2{x}^{4}-7{x}^{3}-15{x}^{2}.$
question.worked_solution:
To find the roots of the polynomial, we must solve the equation $p(x)=0,$ that is

$$
2{x}^{4}-7{x}^{3}-15{x}^{2}=0.
$$

First, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of ${x}^{2}.$ We can factor out the ${x}^{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}(2{x}^{2}-7x-15) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we factor the expression $2{x}^{2}-7x-15$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}(2{x}^{2}-7x-15) & =0 \\ {x}^{2}(2x+3)(x-5) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are $x=0,$ $x=-\frac{3}{2},$ and $x=5.$
